message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a comprehensive overview organized into key categories:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| | Natural abundance | 99.98 % ¹H, 0.02 % ²H, trace ³H |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (¹H), 1 (²H), ½ (³H) |
| | Half‑life of ³H | 12.32 yr |
| **Physical Properties (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈1/14 of air) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.2 cm² s⁻¹ at STP) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (≈0.18 mol L⁻¹) |
| | Vapor pressure | 1 atm at 20.28 K |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides, acids, and many organic compounds |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Acidic behavior | Forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides |
| | Fluorination | H₂ + F₂ → 2 HF (strongly exothermic) |
| | Halogenation | H₂ + Cl₂ → 2 HCl (very exothermic) |
| | Oxidation | H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (combustion) |
| | Reduction | H₂ + CO₂ → CH₄ + H₂O (methanation) |
| | Photochemical behavior | UV light can dissociate H₂ into radicals |
| | Catalytic behavior | Used as a reducing agent in hydrogenation reactions |
| **Nuclear & Isotopic Properties** | Deuterium (²H) | Stable isotope; used in NMR, neutron moderation, heavy water |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive; β‑emitter; used in fusion research, radiolabeling |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) | ¹H NMR is the most widely used spectroscopic technique |
| | Fusion potential | D + T → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV (key reaction in fusion reactors) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells (electricity generation) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen (LH₂/LOX) |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, and other chemicals |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for metal extraction |
| | Medical imaging | ¹H MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen storage in metal hydrides, carbon materials, or pressurized tanks |
| | Environmental | Clean combustion produces only water vapor |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; wide flammability range (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| | Explosion risk | Can form explosive mixtures with air or oxygen |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause asphyxiation by displacing oxygen |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks; careful leak detection |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen’s low mass gives it the highest specific energy (energy per unit mass) among fuels.
- **Diatomic molecule**: Exists naturally as H₂; the H–H bond is relatively weak compared to many other covalent bonds, making it highly reactive.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (¹H) is the most common, but deuterium and tritium have distinct nuclear properties that enable specialized applications (heavy water, fusion, NMR).
- **Electrochemical importance**: Hydrogen is central to electrolysis (splitting water into H₂ and O₂) and fuel cells (combining H₂ with O₂ to produce electricity and water).
- **Environmental friendliness**: Combustion of hydrogen yields only water vapor, making it a clean energy carrier when produced from renewable sources.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
